text:
Hi all,

I am sorry for the confusion that has come up in a few recent animal-travel cases, and I want to reset our tone in internal replies. We need to keep our messages calm, careful, and respectful, especially when a passenger is stressed about pet handling or documents. Please keep checking the welfare notes before you respond, and make sure any follow-up is clear enough for the next teammate who opens the file.

For the Caldreth routing notes, <<FACT F007>> Please do not add extra commentary around that point, and keep the case note focused on what the traveler needs next. If you are sending a handoff to the supervisor, include the comfort concerns, any crate details, and whether the animal has already been reviewed by the welfare coordinator. If something is unclear, flag it early so we can avoid a rushed reply later.

For Port Isolde, <<FACT F015>> Please use that detail exactly as provided and do not restate it in a different form. When you answer a passenger, keep the language simple and steady, and avoid promising anything you have not confirmed. If a traveler is worried about a pet relief stop or arrival handling, acknowledge the concern first and then give the next practical step. That approach has been working better for our team, and it helps us protect both service quality and animal comfort.

Thank you for staying attentive and for helping make our internal communication more consistent.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
